cards.title: Flying with four kids: kindness from strangers
cards.body: A passenger's small act of kindness—tucking a blanket around a sleeping child—transformed a stressful international flight. These moments remind us of the human compassion that can ease parenting challenges.

cards.title: Should you tell children about inheritance surprises?
cards.body: Experts suggest discussing your will's contents with adult children to prevent family conflict. Unexpected inheritance plans can tear families apart if not handled thoughtfully.

cards.title: Family mealtimes: connection kids need
cards.body: Eating together gives parents and children a pause to listen and share stories. Regular mealtimes build meaningful family bonds and mental wellness.

cards.title: Parental tracking apps: surveillance or care?
cards.body: Location-tracking apps let worried parents monitor loved ones' movements, but constant surveillance can damage trust. Finding balance between safety and privacy matters for healthy relationships.

cards.title: Preparing kids for anxiety: expect it happens
cards.body: Teaching children to anticipate fears, rather than waiting passively, builds resilience and coping skills. By normalizing anxiety as part of life, we empower kids to handle it better.

cards.title: New teacher? Your child may learn more
cards.body: A teacher who isn't a perfect fit can actually teach kids cognitive flexibility and resilience. Adapting to change builds valuable life skills early.

cards.title: Maternal ambivalence: mothers carry it all
cards.body: Mothers experience love, anger, joy, and doubt simultaneously—all of it valid. Understanding this complex emotional mix helps reduce parenting guilt and shame.

cards.title: Teaching kids kindness and resisting hate
cards.body: Parents can help children understand difficult emotions while building empathy and courage. Teaching them to practice compassion over cruelty strengthens moral development.

cards.title: Why adult children rehash past grievances
cards.body: An apology alone may not be enough for adult children hurt by past parenting. They're often processing deeper needs for acknowledgment and change, not just words.

cards.title: Young people's mental health rising: experts warn
cards.body: Recent data shows youth mental distress is genuine and increasing, not a sign of weakness. Being young today is harder than previous generations, requiring more parental awareness and support.
